title: Thermal Nociception Threshold at the Paw in Wistar Rats Protocol
author: Ashleigh Abbott
materials: Plug in the response trigger into the corresponding input (labeled “Response”) on the right side of the QST.Lab module. Stimulation surface and thermode for the T10 probe ~0.25 inch diameter QST.Labs T10 Probe (can heat and cool at controlled temperature ranges and rates) QST.Lab Module (TCS II Model)

An ambiguous response to the stimulus is if during or after the ten-second count the rat moves/slightly raises or shakes its leg from the thermode without vocalizing. If a rat has an ambiguous response, repeat the measurement or application of the probe again; record as positive (X) or a negative (O) response along with QST.lab data.

steps.title: Prepare Testing Surface
steps.instruction: Set up the rack shelf with 0.5” x 0.5” metal mesh flooring, ensuring the rack height allows for both placing the rat in the cage and accessing the underside for the probe.

substeps.instruction: Lay the 0.5” x 0.5” metal mesh flooring onto a rack shelf.
Line up the mesh and cages so that the QST probe can fit through both sets of metal bars.
Place cages directly on top of the metal mesh flooring.

steps.title: Configure QST.Lab Module
steps.instruction: Power on the QST.Lab module and configure the experimental parameters for heating and cooling.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the device using the on/off switch on the right side.
Create an experimental protocol to set the temperature range, ramp rate, series of the test, and start/stop settings.
Set heating parameters: baseline of 30°C with temperature ramp increase of 0.5°C/second to 50°C.
Set cooling parameters: baseline of 30°C with temperature ramp decrease of -0.5°C/second to 0°C.

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Animals
steps.instruction: Prepare the probe and acclimate the animals to the environment.

substeps.instruction: Uncap the T10 probe and hold it in the dominant hand; hold the response trigger in the non-dominant hand.
Acclimate rats to the room in their home cages before beginning.
Place rats in the von Frey cage atop the 0.5x0.5” wire mesh flooring.
Allow rats 10-15 minutes to acclimate to the enclosure.

steps.title: Perform Thermal Stimulation
steps.instruction: Execute the thermal testing protocol, starting with the cool protocol first.

substeps.instruction: Load the cool protocol (test for 3 trials before proceeding to heat).
Tap the Start button to begin the countdown.
Place the probe on the midplantar region of the paw, ensuring the thermode element is perpendicular and as flush with the paw surface as possible.
Press the response trigger immediately if a positive response (audible vocalization, visual/reflexive withdrawal, or paw licking) is noted.
If no response occurs within the temperature range (~40-60 seconds), proceed to the next step.
Remove the probe from the paw once a response is noted or the time limit is reached.

steps.title: Record Data and Repeat
steps.instruction: Document the results and repeat the trials according to the experimental design.

substeps.instruction: Record the response as positive (X) or negative (O), noting the specific type of withdrawal (vocalization, visual, or reflexive) and the data from the QST.lab device (response temperature, delta of temp, etc.).
Repeat the stimulation and recording process until 3 trials per temperature are achieved.
Repeat testing for each rat with 30 minutes between each session for a total of 3 sessions per paw for one temperature.
After completing 3 trials per rat for the cool protocol, repeat the process for the heat protocol (3 trials per rat).

steps.title: Post-Procedure
steps.instruction: Return rats to their standard housing cages once testing is complete.
